prompts: Use case: ui-mockup. Create a high fidelity polished UI concept presentation for DiveVault, a personal scuba diving logbook application. Landscape image, large crisp desktop application screen plus a smaller mobile screen alongside, flat front-facing UI, no device hardware, no perspective. Clearly readable typography, production-feasible accessible layouts. This is a design exploration using illustrative sample data. Preserve primary navigation Overview, Logbook, Imports with badge 3, Map, Equipment, Settings. Prominent Add dive and secondary Import actions. Ocean-inspired restrained palette, excellent data clarity, no decorative gradients, no giant vanity statistics, no invented features such as social feeds or AI assistants. Metric units. Distinguish completed dives from pending imported records. Use same sample dive throughout: Blue Hole, Dahab; 24 Oct 2026; 42 min; max depth 28.4 m; buddy Maya Chen. Other rows: Canyon, Dahab; Lighthouse Reef. Missing measurements shown as em dash. Chart where shown is explicitly illustrative recorded depth profile with time/min and depth/m axes. Include a small outside-the-app caption 'Concept study · illustrative data'. Render one coherent visual design, not a collage of alternatives. Concept 01 — Coastal Ledger. Light airy utilitarian product design: off-white canvas, white surfaces, slate navy typography, one teal primary action color, fine gray rules, modern humanist sans-serif, restrained corner radius. Desktop Logbook screen: compact vertical left sidebar with DiveVault wordmark and navigation, main title Logbook with subtitle '126 completed dives', Add dive and Import actions. Slim pending callout '3 imported dives need review' and Review imports link. Search plus Site and Buddy filter controls. Beautiful generous semantic table columns Dive, Date, Site, Buddy, Duration, Max depth, with selected Blue Hole row and several other rows. Right detail preview pane for Blue Hole with modest depth chart, key metrics, notes 'Quiet descent along the reef wall.', View dive button. Mobile companion shows Logbook as legible cards, same Blue Hole data, Add dive action and bottom navigation Overview, Logbook, Imports, More. Small concept title outside screens: '01 / Coastal Ledger'. Emphasize calm organization and fast scanning.

Clearly readable typography, production-feasible accessible layouts. This is a design exploration using illustrative sample data. Preserve primary navigation Overview, Logbook, Imports with badge 3, Map, Equipment, Settings. Prominent Add dive and secondary Import actions. Ocean-inspired restrained palette, excellent data clarity, no decorative gradients, no giant vanity statistics, no invented features such as social feeds or AI assistants. Metric units. Distinguish completed dives from pending imported records. Use same sample dive throughout: Blue Hole, Dahab; 24 Oct 2026; 42 min; max depth 28.4 m; buddy Maya Chen. Dark technical but approachable dive-computer inspired UI: charcoal blue canvas, slightly lighter navy panels, cool white readable type, muted gray secondary text, one clear aqua primary action color, amber only for pending status. Monospace numerals paired with clean sans-serif labels; no neon glow, no excessive roundness. Desktop dive detail screen with thin vertical left primary navigation, Logbook active; breadcrumb Logbook / Blue Hole; large but restrained Blue Hole title, Dahab and 24 Oct 2026. Add dive and Import visible in top header. Main two-thirds shows wide recorded depth profile with visible metric axes, subtle grid, shaded aqua area, four concise metrics 42 min / 28.4 m max / 16.2 m average / 25 °C water. Below: notes and buddy Maya Chen, collapsed equipment section. Right one-third contains compact 'Dive details' panel with source 'Dive computer', conditions visibility '15 m', pending queue card '3 imported dives need review'. Avoid tank editing controls or unsupported service history. Mobile companion displays the same dive detail with depth plot, metric grid and Notes, clear back navigation, Edit logbook button. Small concept title outside screens: '02 / Deep Instrument'. Strong hierarchy and legibility, professional instrument feel.
